cohort: The study included all women who delivered vaginally or via cesarean section between 2008 and 2024 at the University Medical Center Ljubljana, Slovenia, and subsequently required medical assessment or hospitalization within six weeks postpartum.
finding: Postpartum complications were observed in 7.6 % of women following vaginal birth and 10.6 % after cesarean delivery, with infections and breastfeeding-related problems being the most common reasons for medical reevaluation.
mod_finding: Postpartum complications were more frequent after cesarean delivery (10.6 %) than vaginal birth (7.6 %), with surgical site complications predominating after cesarean section and breast complications or minor perineal issues more common after vaginal birth.
